report: L1 / Proxy, Three.js sampled-frame baseline. I read the complete prompt and manifest and visually inspected all 24 supplied JPEG samples, spanning frame 0 through frame 383. The scene uses two persistent articulated geometric people, a dark coat with two editable broad deformable tails, three pistol proxies, a rooftop, coarse surrounding buildings, a service enclosure, a background helicopter, and procedural projectile air wakes and haze. The black-coated man's two guns lower and fall, his knees bend and torso arches backward while his arms change pose, and he subsequently falls into the final overhead composition. The suited man remains opposite him with an articulated aiming arm. Camera cuts cover the opening suited close shot, frontal two-pistol shot, muzzle close-up, long rear shot and continuous orbit, two inferred impact inserts, and the overhead ending. Timing is absolute and deterministic on the original 23.976023976 fps, 384-frame, 16.016-second timeline; the injected resolution and aspect ratio are respected. The observed samples establish the broad actions and compositions. Cut boundaries between samples, intersample motion, projectile counts and trajectories, hidden joint positions, helicopter placement, and cloth motion are inferred, not directly observed. This is the first and only generation: no scene execution, rendering, render feedback, testing, or refinement was performed. Exact camera calibration, contact accuracy, lighting, depth of field, motion blur, intermediate action timing, and executable/rendered appearance remain unverified. Fine faces, clothing, textures, and effects are intentionally simplified for L1. No scores or equivalence to Blender model rankings are claimed.
